title: Statement Cycle Note: The Part of the Balance a Payment Plan Covers
content:
A payment plan on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program does not always cover the whole balance, because recent postings are still being billed in the regular statement cycle.

**Note.** The plan covers the program's balance less the patient charges posted on it within the last calendar month when such charges are on file, because those charges are still within their first statement's terms; it covers only the program's aged balance when no such charges are on file and the program carries an aged balance above 0 together with postings made within the last 4 calendar months, because the newer postings are still billed in the regular statement cycle; and otherwise it covers the program's balance; a date falls within the last calendar month when it is later than the same calendar day one month earlier.

**The aged balance.** The aged balance is the program's postings dated more than 4 calendar months before today less all of its payments and balance adjustments, never below 0, a posting being that old when its posting date is not later than the same calendar day 4 months earlier. The postings are the program's remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds.

**Cases (hypothetical account; today is 15 September)**

| Account | Plan covers |
|---|---|
| balance 300.00, including a patient charge of 40.00 posted 5 September | 260.00 |
| no charge in the last month; postings of 200.00 dated 1 March and 100.00 dated 20 July; payments of 50.00 | aged balance 200.00 less 50.00, that is 150.00 |
| no charge in the last month; all postings dated on or before 15 May; balance 180.00 | 180.00, the balance — no postings in the last 4 months |
| no charge in the last month; payments exceed the old postings, so the aged balance is 0 | the balance |

**Boundary of "aged".** On 15 September a posting dated 15 May is aged; one dated 16 May is a posting of the last 4 calendar months.
